## createFromUrl

Create Attachment From Url. `POST /attachments/from-url`

Fetch a public URL server-side and store it as an attachment.

Returns the same shape as POST /upload so the response is interchangeable. Caller can then pass the returned id / attachment_id in MessageCreate.attachments.

```php
$result = $sendseven->attachments()->createFromUrl(url: 'url');
```

- Scopes: `messages:create`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$url` | `string` | yes | Public http(s) URL to fetch. file://, gopher://, etc. are rejected. Hostnames resolving to private/loopback/link-local IPs are blocked (SSRF protection). |
| `$filename` | `?string` | no | Optional override for the stored filename. If omitted, the filename is derived from the URL path, falling back to a UUID-based name. |
| `$idempotencyKey` | `?string` | no | Repeat a request safely: SendSeven answers a repeat with the first result. One is generated when omitted. |

Returns `AttachmentUpload`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Attachments/create_attachment_from_url_api_v1_attachments_from_url_post)

## delete

Delete Attachment. `DELETE /attachments/{attachment_id}`

Delete an attachment

Permanently removes the attachments row and its stored blob. This is irreversible. Attachments are re-usable and carry no foreign key back to the messages that referenced them, so deleting one that a previously sent message still points at is allowed and expected — the message keeps its metadata, the media simply stops resolving.

```php
$sendseven->attachments()->delete(attachmentId: 'attachment_id');
```

- Scopes: `messages:delete`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$attachmentId` | `string` | yes |  |

Returns `void`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Attachments/delete_attachment_api_v1_attachments__attachment_id__delete)
